## CONVERGING target contract — runtime alignment pending

This page is the single current design authority for SCNSim automatic semantic
circuit diagrams. It supersedes earlier presentation prose about page-wide
rails, first-Port paths, opaque Composite fallbacks, `SchematicPath`,
`SchematicGroup`, and packing groups.

The target interfaces and fail-closed audits described here are **not yet the
current runtime implementation**. Full V1 numerical, workspace, and identity
semantics remain `STABILIZED`; only this diagram-presentation scope is
`CONVERGING`. Human review of this document precedes runtime/API alignment and
durable stabilization tests.
:::

## Product promise

An automatic diagram is useful for Agent-authored circuits only when it does
more than look plausible. A successful `CircuitDiagramResult` must certify
that the visible electrical and semantic projection can be reconstructed and
matched exactly to the `CircuitPlan` snapshot from which it was made.

The promise has three deliberately separate parts:

| Audit | Question | Product responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| A. Electrical fidelity | Do the emitted symbols, pins, wires, ground returns, Ports, and coupled branches reconstruct the exact Plan connectivity? | Mandatory independent renderer audit. |
| B. Semantic fidelity | Do the visible Subsystems, parallel relations, interfaces, differential bundles, and mutual couplings reconstruct the intended presentation IR? | Mandatory independent renderer audit and complete visual alphabet. |
| C. Design intent | Is this exact Plan the circuit the Human intended the Agent to build? | Human review of the certified diagram and review table. |

Passing A and B means that the diagram does not lie about the Plan. It does not
mean that the Plan itself satisfies a Design Target. SCNSim must not describe C
as an automated validation result.

## Authority and snapshot identity

`CircuitPlan` remains the only physical-authoring authority. Layout objects,
diagram geometry, labels, SVG metadata, and audit tables cannot declare a
component, split a net, add a pin, or change canonical ground.

`render_schematic()` captures the same canonical Plan document and SHA-256
encoding used when a later `CircuitRun` seals the Plan. Capturing that immutable
snapshot does not seal or mutate a Plan that is still being authored. If the
Plan changes afterward, the old diagram continues to identify the old
snapshot; a new render receives a new Plan SHA. A diagram and an analysis
result refer to the same physical Plan only when their complete
`plan_sha256` values agree.

The Plan SHA binds the physical baseline declaration, including component
hierarchy, topology, the canonical union of grounded endpoints, parameters,
source-unit provenance, Ports, and couplings. Separate `ground()` call groups
may remain diagram/audit evidence without entering the physical Plan hash;
they can therefore change the connectivity certificate's ground-group record
without claiming a different simulated circuit. Presentation choices never
enter Plan identity.

## One semantic projection pipeline

Authoring and compiled diagrams use one certified pipeline with two independent
branches:

```text
canonical Plan snapshot
├─> independent expected electrical and semantic manifests
└─> semantic lowering -> placement -> routing -> actual emitted geometry
                                      ├─> electrical reconstruction audit (A)
                                      └─> semantic reconstruction audit (B)
                                                       |
                                              Theme / SVG serialization
```

The expected manifests are derived directly from the canonical Plan document.
The observed manifests are reconstructed after placement from the objects that
were actually emitted. The reconstruction code may read only:

- native-symbol types and their transformed electrical anchors;
- CPW/MTL boundary anchors and conductor rows;
- conductive segment endpoints;
- Port boundary, circuit, and load anchors;
- ground-glyph attachment buses;
- T-junction and wire-jump geometry;
- RelationBlock terminals; and
- visible IDs, parameter labels, and coupling marks.

It must not reuse the manifest or bundle enumeration that drove placement. One
lowered table cannot be both the drawing instruction and its own witness.
Hidden SVG metadata may carry provenance, but it cannot repair an incomplete
visible projection or satisfy either audit.

## Semantic layout IR

The private IR separates electrical identity from drawing geometry.

### ElementBlock

Every physical R, L, C, G, Josephson junction, and junction capacitance is an
orientation-aware native `ElementBlock`. A block owns:

- the full component path and primitive kind;
- ordered physical pins and electrical anchors;
- the native Schemdraw symbol bounds;
- separately measured name and baseline-value label rows; and
- one occupied bounding box that includes the required clearances.

Native labels are attached to their oriented symbols. They are not placed as
free-floating text after layout, and label width never stretches the
electrical symbol. Horizontal elements use top or bottom label regions;
vertical elements use the measured outside left or right region appropriate to
their direction. Name and value are measured as separate rows with at least
`1/8 U` between their occupied bounds.

### SubsystemBlock

A `SubsystemBlock` preserves component hierarchy, attachment ownership, and
relative packing. It is normally invisible: SCNSim does not replace a
resonator, IDC, SQUID, or custom Composite with a generic rectangle. Each
Subsystem ID is shown once, while native leaves use the shortest unique local
name plus a separate value row. Full canonical component paths remain
available in audit evidence and `run.explain()`.

Every built-in and user-authored Composite recursively expands its sealed
snapshot into native R/L/C/G/JJ symbols. Hidden child handles remain
unavailable to authoring code even though the sealed physical branches are
visible. CPW/MTL transmission line is the only boxed custom electrical symbol.

### RelationBlock

Parallel leaves with the same unordered endpoint pair form one
`RelationBlock`. Examples include C parallel with L and a Josephson junction
parallel with its Cj. A RelationBlock owns its two terminal buses, native
leaves, labels, and any local ground glyph. It prevents parallel branches from
being placed as a false series chain.

### InterfaceBundle and attachments

An `InterfaceBundle` is derived from the Plan; it is not a second topology
declaration. It groups the top-level primitive or relation members that connect
two Subsystems, or that connect a Port boundary to one Subsystem.
Its canonical Plan-derived identity is visible exactly once in the diagram and
is the identity reconstructed by the semantic audit.

Attachment geometry is decided per Public `ElectricNode`, not from the total
number of neighbors of a whole Subsystem:

- one single-ended bundle receives one centered outward anchor;
- two single-ended bundles receive opposite inline anchors on the same node;
- three or more bundles receive ordered anchors on a short boundary bus; and
- a bundle touching several Public nodes is differential or multi-terminal,
  so its terminals face the peer Subsystem together as a set.

Top-level two-terminal primitives bridging two Subsystem public nodes belong
to that interface. Canonical ground is never counted as a neighboring
Subsystem. No attachment rule may invent another ElectricNode or public pin.

### NetBus and NetTap

One `ElectricNode` may need several geometric contacts. The layout may
therefore create one private `NetBus` with several private `NetTap` anchors.
All taps reconstruct to the same electrical node. A labeled Public node has
one identity anchor and one filled dot; ordinary taps and T-junctions are
unfilled. A Port-promoted node is identified by its open Port circle rather
than a second node dot.

## Complete visual alphabet

### Native branches and ground

R, L, C, G, Josephson junctions, and Cj are drawn with native electrical
symbols. IDC is shown as its terminal-to-terminal capacitance plus both
terminal-to-reference shunts. Grounded and floating resonators expose their
actual parallel branches. A SQUID exposes both junctions, each Cj, and finite
loop inductance.

Parallel grounded branches attached to the same signal node and ground group
share a short local bottom bus and one ground glyph. Shunts belonging to
different signal nodes receive separate ground glyphs even though every glyph
maps to the one canonical Plan ground. Canonical ground is never a page-wide
layout vertex or rail.

### CPW and MTL

One-conductor transmission line is an inline CPW box with continuous outline,
input/output anchors, ID, and length. Multi-conductor line is one MTL box with
ordered conductor rows and one head/tail anchor per row. The reference
conductor is explicit legend metadata and never creates an inferred ground
wire.

The compiled projection expands every line into its complete pi ladder. For
N>1 it preserves matrix order and complete C/G and L/R evidence rather than
inventing scalar equivalents.

### Logical Ports

A logical Port is one rotatable presentation block containing:

- an open boundary circle;
- an interior circuit anchor;
- an unfilled interior T-junction;
- the declared reference-impedance branch and local ground; and
- a visible Port ID, role, and baseline Z0.

`terminated` and `nonloading_probe` are visibly distinct; the latter is marked
PTC-removable. The load branch is the existing raw-network Port load, not an
authored Library resistor. On an interior horizontal bus the Port block faces
top or bottom; on an interior vertical bus it faces left or right. Endpoint
Ports may remain tangent to the bus.

### Junctions and crossings

- A filled dot denotes one labeled Public-node identity.
- An ordinary same-net T-junction is unfilled.
- A same-net four-way meeting becomes two staggered T-junctions.
- Different nets never use an ordinary cross; an unavoidable crossing uses a
  wire jump.
- Wires may enter or leave blocks only through registered anchors and may not
  cross a symbol, label, Port block, or Subsystem occupied region.

### Mutual inductance

When both inductors participate only in one coupling and can remain adjacent
without changing public-terminal order or violating occupied boxes, they are
drawn as adjacent parallel inductors with signed `k` between them and derived
`M` when values are visible.

Otherwise the diagram contains a non-optional coupling legend that identifies
both oriented branch paths, signed `k`, and optional derived `M`. A mutual
coupling with neither an adjacent mark nor a complete visible legend fails the
semantic audit. Drawing placement never determines the physical sign.

## Automatic placement and routing

All geometry derives from one private diagram metric system with
`unit_length = 2.2` Schemdraw coordinates:

| Quantity | Minimum |
|---|---|
| Native element span | `1 U` |
| Label clearance | `1/8 U` |
| Terminal stub and wire obstacle clearance | `1/4 U` |
| Routing-lane pitch | `1/2 U` |
| Port lead | `5/8 U` |
| Port load span | `1 U` |
| Grounded-branch depth | `2 U` |
| Disconnected-panel gap | `3 U` |

Measured symbol, label, legend, and provenance bounds may only increase these
spacings. No fixture ID, Tutorial name, component ID, hand-authored coordinate,
or public scale knob may bypass the metric system.

Each connected panel is decomposed into articulation and biconnected blocks.
All distinct `terminated` Ports participate in the connecting backbone;
`nonloading_probe` Ports remain peripheral. A panel with fewer than two
terminated Ports roots at the first Port or earliest Public node. Cycles remain
biconnected semantic blocks rather than being broken by an arbitrary pairwise
path. Disconnected circuits are packed as separate panels.

Placement reserves complete ElementBlock, RelationBlock, InterfaceBundle,
Port, label, and legend bounds. Rows, columns, boundary buses, and routing lanes
expand monotonically until all accepted constraints hold. Deterministic Plan
declaration order and exact IDs are tie breakers. The heuristic does not claim
a global optimum.

## Relational manual hints

Manual layout is a constrained reading-order input to the same automatic
engine. It is not a coordinate escape hatch. All of the following target types
are exported from the `scnsim` package root; the definitions show their public
shape rather than a second implementation module:

```python
from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from types import MappingProxyType

class DiagramSide(str, Enum):
    LEFT = "left"
    RIGHT = "right"
    TOP = "top"
    BOTTOM = "bottom"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SchematicInterface:
    id: str
    members: tuple[ComponentInstance, ...] = ()
    nodes: tuple[ElectricNodeRef, ...] = ()

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SchematicAttachment:
    interface: SchematicInterface
    at: ComponentInstance | ElectricNodeRef

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SchematicRoute:
    points: tuple[PortRef | SchematicAttachment, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SchematicLayout:
    interfaces: tuple[SchematicInterface, ...] = ()
    primary_routes: tuple[SchematicRoute, ...] = ()
    attachment_sides: Mapping[SchematicAttachment, DiagramSide] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({})
    )
    attachment_order: Mapping[
        ComponentInstance | ElectricNodeRef,
        tuple[SchematicAttachment, ...],
    ] = field(default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({}))
    port_sides: Mapping[PortRef, DiagramSide] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({})
    )
```

`DiagramSide` is the only accepted side value; raw strings fail before layout.
Every mapping is defensively copied into an immutable, deterministic internal
mapping during construction, so a caller retaining the original dictionary
cannot mutate a layout after validation.

`SchematicInterface.id` is a nonempty layout-local selector identity. It is
unique within one `SchematicLayout`, but it is neither a new Plan identity nor
an alias for an ElectricNode or InterfaceBundle. The automatic IR's canonical
bundle identity remains the visible semantic identifier and digest input.
Changing only the selector ID therefore cannot change the certified semantic
manifest.

`members` and `nodes` cannot both be empty. Their combined selector is an
intersection and must match exactly one InterfaceBundle already derived from
the same Plan. Each `members` entry is a top-level `ComponentInstance`; each
`nodes` entry is a Public `ElectricNodeRef`. Nodes disambiguate genuine
multi-terminal relations; they do not declare a net or route. Two interface
selectors may not select the same derived bundle.

An attachment selects exactly one existing public/top-level endpoint of its
interface. A component endpoint means the bundle's attachment to that
Subsystem; a node endpoint means its attachment at that Public node. If `at`
matches neither or more than one endpoint, validation fails.

A route contains at least two distinct points and defines only primary reading
order. Every consecutive point pair must already have one unique connecting
chain in the automatic semantic IR; an absent or ambiguous chain fails rather
than being guessed. A caller resolves a cyclic ambiguity by adding existing
intermediate attachments until every adjacent route hop is unique, never by
supplying coordinates. An attachment cannot occupy conflicting positions in
two primary routes. `attachment_sides`, `attachment_order`, and `port_sides`
constrain only eligible outer anchors and cannot make a nonadjacent pair
adjacent electrically.

All referenced handles must belong to the same Plan. Hidden or internal leaves,
foreign handles, duplicate interfaces, incomplete endpoints, conflicting
orders, impossible sides, and a selector that matches zero or several bundles
raise `SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_layout")`. Compiled diagrams
reject authoring layout hints with `ValueError`.

`layout=None` and hinted layouts pass through the same placement, routing, and
independent audits. They must produce identical connectivity and semantic
digests. When runtime alignment begins, these types replace `SchematicPath`,
`SchematicGroup`, and `branch_order` completely; there is no alias, compatibility
encoder, or migration path.

## Independent audits and digests

### Electrical reconstruction (A)

The observed electrical manifest normalizes:

- every native branch kind, full path, ordered pin, and reconstructed net;
- every ground return and local-group membership;
- every Port attachment, role, Z0, and node-to-reference orientation;
- every CPW/MTL conductor, reference, head/tail attachment, and row order;
- every mutually coupled oriented branch pair; and
- every exact-zero branch omitted from visible geometry.

Its canonical digest is `connectivity_sha256`. The observed manifest must
equal the independently generated expected manifest exactly; set equality
without complete ordered-pin and orientation evidence is insufficient.

### Semantic reconstruction (B)

The observed semantic manifest reconstructs:

- Subsystem hierarchy and each visible Subsystem identity;
- RelationBlock endpoints and native members;
- InterfaceBundle endpoints, member branches, and single-ended versus
  differential/multi-terminal classification;
- Port-boundary ownership; and
- mutual-coupling presentation mode and visible identity.

Its canonical digest is `semantic_sha256`. A parallel relation drawn as series,
a differential interface drawn as unrelated single-ended branches, an omitted
coupling mark, or an ambiguous ownership label fails this audit even when
electrical connectivity happens to be correct. Adjacent-inductor and visible-
legend coupling presentations normalize to the same coupling identity; their
geometric presentation mode is audit evidence but is not part of the semantic
digest.

### Geometry and label validity

Before semantic serialization, layout validation proves that occupied blocks
and labels do not overlap, wires contact only registered anchors, conductive
paths are continuous, and junction/jump grammar is unambiguous. When baseline
values are visible, their rendered labels must exactly match the canonical
Plan values and source-unit provenance selected for display.

Theme, hint choice, provenance visibility, padding, and equivalent geometric
routing are excluded from the Plan, connectivity, and semantic digest
preimages. Each digest uses a schema-tagged canonical encoding so a future
meaning change cannot silently reuse an old digest.

## Target Result and presentation surface

The target defaults make an ordinary authoring diagram review-ready:

```python
CircuitDiagramSpec(
    *,
    representation="authoring",
    theme=Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values=True,
    show_provenance=True,
    layout: SchematicLayout | None = None,
)
```

Successful construction attaches an immutable audit with no public
constructor. The following is its read-only protocol, not a user-constructible
dataclass:

```python
class CircuitDiagramAudit:
    @property
    def representation(self) -> Literal["authoring", "compiled"]: ...

    @property
    def plan_id(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def plan_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def connectivity_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def semantic_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def compiled_graph_sha256(self) -> str | None: ...

    def show(self) -> HtmlPresentation: ...

diagram.audit.plan_sha256
diagram.audit.connectivity_sha256
diagram.audit.semantic_sha256
diagram.audit.compiled_graph_sha256
diagram.audit.show()
```

There is no `passed` boolean: failure returns no diagram or audit object.
`CircuitDiagramResult.show()` continues to return the real Schemdraw `Drawing`.
Notebook rich display continues to provide the self-contained copy, zoom,
reset, drag-pan, and Open SVG surface. Static SVG/raster save remains a
non-interactive projection.

### Provenance region

A measured bottom region and outer padding keep all symbols and labels away
from the image boundary. By default the region displays:

```text
AUTHORING · CircuitPlan <id> · plan <12> · conn <12> · semantic <12> · values: baseline
```

A compiled diagram additionally displays `compiled <12>`. The region uses the
same Theme palette as the drawing. Complete digests remain in
`CircuitDiagramAudit` and SVG metadata; neither independent audit relies on
that metadata.

`show_provenance=False` removes the visible region but never disables the
audits or typed certificate. A copied raster without the region consequently
has no standalone visible provenance; this is an explicit presentation choice.

### Audit review table

`diagram.audit.show()` displays the audited observed reconstruction rather than
printing the Plan's expected manifest a second time. It contains:

- Plan identity and full digests;
- Public nodes, exact endpoints, and ground groups;
- Ports, roles, Z0, and orientation;
- InterfaceBundle endpoints and members;
- RelationBlock endpoints and native leaves;
- mutual-coupling branch identities, signed `k`, and derived `M` when defined;
- CPW/MTL conductor order, reference, and head/tail attachments;
- omitted-zero declarations; and
- baseline values with source-unit provenance.

For a compiled projection it also includes the expanded graph identity, line
sections, conductor/station identities, complete matrix evidence, and omitted
compiled zero terms.

## Compiled projection

Compiled diagrams perform two certified comparisons:

```text
Plan snapshot -> compiler expanded graph -> expected compiled manifest
                                  actual compiled drawing
                                           -> observed compiled manifest
```

The Plan SHA proves the source; `compiled_graph_sha256` proves the exact
expansion; the reconstructed connectivity and semantic digests prove the
visible compiled drawing. A large ladder may use deterministic pages or
panels, but it cannot truncate sections, conductor rows, matrix entries,
attachments, or omitted-zero evidence.

Compiled projection remains structural baseline evidence. It contains no PTC,
retain, transform, Schur reduction, Direct/HB response, or ParameterSet
override. Those request-specific facts belong to `run.explain()` and verified
analysis Results.

## Fail-closed behavior

Layout cannot return a degraded or partial image. These are
`schematic_layout` failures:

- malformed, foreign, ambiguous, or contradictory manual hints;
- an unplaceable required visual mark or provenance region;
- symbol, Port, label, legend, or panel overlap;
- a wire entering a non-anchor obstacle;
- a disconnected required wire segment; or
- an ambiguous ordinary crossing that cannot be represented with the junction
  and jump alphabet.

These are `schematic_audit` failures:

- expected and reconstructed pins, nets, ground, Ports, or line conductors
  differ;
- a branch is missing, duplicated, reversed, or attached to the wrong net;
- RelationBlock, InterfaceBundle, Subsystem, or differential classification
  differs;
- a required coupling or omission record is not visibly and completely
  represented; or
- a visible baseline name/value label disagrees with the captured Plan.

No warning-only path, page-wide-rail fallback, hidden metadata repair, or
best-effort success is allowed.

## Human review protocol

An Agent submitting a `CircuitPlan` supplies a code-free review packet:

1. the default authoring diagram with baseline values and provenance visible;
2. the Net/BOM table from `diagram.audit.show()`;
3. a compiled diagram and compiled audit table whenever CPW/MTL or another
   compiler expansion is present; and
4. the applicable Design Target against which the Human judges intent.

Machine audit guarantees A and B. The Human uses the certified visual grammar
to decide C: whether the topology, Subsystems, interfaces, Port roles,
couplings, and baseline quantities are the intended circuit.

## Honest limits

- Diagram values are Plan baselines, not values from a particular
  `ParameterSet`, optimizer candidate, or HB case.
- Authoring and compiled diagrams show the physical Plan. They do not show a
  selected View, PTC compensation, retain, transform, Schur elimination, or
  normalization choice.
- A diagram cannot accept an optimization result, scientific Gate, or Design
  Target.
- `run.explain()` remains the authority for request-specific lowering and
  evidence; it cannot substitute for a visible coupling mark or repair a
  failed diagram audit.
- Matrix RLGC requires its complete compiled table/legend to be reviewed; the
  CPW/MTL authoring box alone is intentionally insufficient.
- Router stress graphs are diagnostic inputs, not product circuit fixtures or
  examples of physical intent.

## Supersession and implementation order

This document is the only current target authority for the affected scope.
The existing renderer and old public hint classes remain temporarily reachable
only because this is a documentation-first convergence checkpoint. After the
Human accepts the written contract, runtime alignment must:

1. replace the old hint API without aliases or a compatibility encoder;
2. implement the real certified projection and typed audit surface;
3. remove superseded rail, opaque-Composite, packing-group, and best-effort
   paths;
4. validate with ephemeral probes and Human-visible diagrams; and
5. add durable tests only after Human acceptance of the exact implementation
   candidate.

Until that alignment is complete, current rendered diagrams must not be
described as satisfying this target contract.
